response:
Diagnosis from the archive: every additive SUMRANK composite (gen 0 and most of gen 1) produced respectable FMB t-stats (3.1–4.2) but FF5 alphas of roughly zero or the wrong sign — the spread's long leg is value/low-investment and its short leg is growth/high-investment, so HML and CMA absorb the return. The one construction that delivered a real FF5 alpha (ValueConditionedBalanceSheetAccrual: +2.5%/yr, t=2.3) was the *value-gated* multiplicative form in which both legs are cheap stocks and factor loadings cancel. Its weaknesses were a lower FMB t (2.54) and a poor Sharpe (0.20), consistent with an unstable, industry-tilted portfolio. This batch therefore (i) keeps the value-neutral multiplicative architecture but varies the *economic content* of the accrual leg and the *deflator*, (ii) tests the reverse conditioning direction (accrual-quality gate on value) to learn which side carries the interaction, (iii) adds an industry-neutral version to attack the low Sharpe, and (iv) adds one genuinely new price-deflated accrual-overhang mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ValuePremiumGatedByCleanAccruals
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The value premium exists only where reported fundamentals are trustworthy: among clean-accrual firms cheapness predicts high returns, while among accrual-inflated firms book value is unreliable and the value spread should be flat or perverse.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This inverts the conditioning of the archive's only alpha-positive signal — accrual quality becomes the bounded gate and signed cheapness carries direction — so the long-short spread is long cheap-clean versus short expensive-clean, holding accounting quality high in both legs. Comparing its alpha to ValueConditionedBalanceSheetAccrual identifies whether the interaction is a value effect concentrated in clean firms or an accrual effect concentrated in cheap firms, which is the single most informative unresolved design question in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: PercentAccrualGatedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), ABS(ib))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters for a high earnings yield is the share of that income which is accrual rather than cash, so accruals should be deflated by the magnitude of earnings, not by assets; a cheap-on-earnings firm whose income is mostly accrual is a trap regardless of its asset base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Scaling accruals by absolute earnings makes the accrual leg commensurate with the earnings-yield valuation leg, so the interaction measures the reliability of the very quantity being capitalized, unlike asset-scaled accruals which mix in capital intensity. This isolates the deflator design choice against the gen-1 winner while switching the valuation channel from book-to-market to earnings yield, giving a cleaner economic reading of "cheap on earnings that are actually cash."
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AccrualOverhangToPrice
EXPRESSION: NEG(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual distortions accumulate as a stock of unrealized working-capital investment; what determines the return drag is the size of that accumulated overhang relative to the firm's market value, since a given dollar of pending reversal is far more damaging for a low-priced firm.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Deflating a five-year cumulative accrual flow by market capitalization rather than assets creates a true valuation-accrual interaction inside a single ratio: the same accounting distortion scores worse when the market values the firm cheaply, which is exactly the value-trap channel. It is structurally different from every archive entry (stock rather than flow, price rather than asset deflator, single ratio rather than composite), so it tests whether the effect is about accrual magnitude per dollar of price.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: IndustryNeutralValueAccrualGate
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Normal working-capital intensity and normal valuation multiples both vary by industry, so cross-sectional accrual and value ranks partly sort industries; purging industry means should keep the same firm-level interaction while removing sector bets that add volatility without alpha.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-1 winner produced a reliable FF5 alpha but a Sharpe of only 0.20, the signature of a spread whose volatility comes from unintended sector concentration rather than from the accounting mechanism. Industry-relative construction on both legs should preserve alpha while cutting spread volatility, so this is a targeted portfolio-diagnostic refinement rather than a new economic claim.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: ValueWithGrossOperatingBalanceSheetChurn
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(ADD(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), sale))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Sloan accruals net asset-side buildup against liability-side buildup, but for a cheap firm both are bad news: growing receivables and inventory signal unsold or uncollected revenue, while growing payables and accrued liabilities signal stretched suppliers and funding strain, so the two should enter with the same sign rather than opposite signs.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a decomposition test of the accrual leg itself: if the netted Sloan measure works only because of its asset side, then a gross-churn version that also penalizes operating-liability expansion should perform at least as well among value stocks and better in the distress tail. Sales scaling keeps both components commensurate with operating volume and avoids the capital-intensity contamination of asset scaling.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ValueWithPersistentlyCleanAccruals
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at)), 0), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: A single year of low accruals can be luck or a one-off working-capital release; a multi-year record of income-decreasing accruals reveals a conservative reporting policy, and cheap firms with such a record are the ones whose book value can be trusted.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This repairs the failure of ValueWithStableWorkingCapital, whose FF5 alpha was significantly negative (−3.4%/yr, t = −3.5) partly because VOL over five annual points is a very noisy second moment and raw wcap measures cash-holding variability rather than accounting policy. Counting the number of clean-accrual years is a robust persistence statistic on a properly cash-excluded accrual measure, testing whether reporting-policy consistency, rather than accrual dispersion, is what distinguishes real value from value traps.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE ValuePremiumGatedByCleanAccruals---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It uses exactly the same two ingredients and functional form as the archive's ValueConditionedBalanceSheetAccrual with the gate/direction roles permuted, which is close to a variant but does produce a genuinely different long-short composition (cheap-clean vs expensive-clean) and answers a well-posed attribution question, so it is worth one test but should not spawn further permutations.

---CRITIQUE PercentAccrualGatedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The earnings-deflated accrual leg is essentially the published "percent accruals" measure (Hafzalla, Lundholm, Van Winkle), so novelty rests only on the earnings-yield gating, and the ABS(ib) denominator will be explosive for near-zero-earnings firms even after winsorization — but the sign logic is internally consistent and the deflator comparison against the gen-1 winner is a legitimate design test.

---CRITIQUE AccrualOverhangToPrice---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: TS_SUM of annual DELTAs telescopes into a plain five-year level change (so the "stock vs flow" novelty claim is vacuous), and dividing a fundamental quantity by market cap makes the signal dominated by the 1/price denominator, i.e. a repackaged value/accrual-to-price ratio rather than a genuine value-accrual interaction.

---CRITIQUE IndustryNeutralValueAccrualGate---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a standard industry-demeaning of the archive's gen-1 winner with no new economic content, and dropping the WINSOR from the z-scored accrual leg leaves it more outlier-exposed than the original, so any Sharpe gain would be a cosmetic robustness result rather than an advance in mechanism.

---CRITIQUE ValueWithGrossOperatingBalanceSheetChurn---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: A clearly motivated decomposition test that deliberately breaks Sloan's netting (asset and liability buildup entering with the same sign) with a sales deflator that is commensurate across both components; the sign structure matches the hypothesis and the economic claim about payables stretching is contestable but genuinely testable.

---CRITIQUE ValueWithPersistentlyCleanAccruals---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Replacing a noisy five-point volatility with a persistence count of income-decreasing-accrual years is a substantive, well-diagnosed repair of the failed ValueWithStableWorkingCapital rather than a cosmetic variant, though the 0–5 integer signal discards magnitude information and requires six years of annual data, so watch coverage and coarse-tercile instability.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ValueWithWorkingCapitalOffItsPeak
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual bloat is a state, not a flow: a cheap firm whose non-cash working-capital intensity now sits far below its own five-year peak has already absorbed and reversed its accrual excess, so its depressed earnings are the trough rather than the start of a decline, whereas a cheap firm sitting at its own peak still has the reversal ahead of it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The telescoping and 1/price problems are both removed: distance-from-own-peak is a genuine level state that cannot collapse into a five-year difference, and no fundamental is divided by market cap, so the signal is not a repackaged accrual-to-price ratio. It retains the value-gated multiplicative architecture because that is the only form in the archive that produced a reliable FF5 alpha (both legs are cheap stocks so HML and CMA cancel), while the accrual content — reversal stage measured against the firm's own history — is new relative to level, gross-churn, percent, and persistence versions already queued.
REASONING: Sales scaling keeps the working-capital state comparable across firm size and avoids capital-intensity contamination.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DeratingWithCleanAccrualSurprise
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp), 1)), dp), at), 3))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What identifies a value trap is not a low valuation level but a *de-rating* accompanied by deteriorating accounting: when a firm becomes cheap relative to its own valuation history while its accruals rise above their own multi-year norm, the price decline is confirmation of fundamental erosion; when the same de-rating occurs with accruals below their own norm, it is sentiment-driven mispricing that reverts.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Both legs are benchmarked to the firm's own history — a time-series cheapness position and an accrual surprise relative to its own three-year average — so the construction is industry- and business-model-free by design rather than by mechanical demeaning, and it adds new economic content (de-rating dynamics interacted with accrual deterioration) instead of re-scaling the gen-1 winner. The accrual leg is winsorized before z-scoring, fixing the outlier exposure the critic identified.
REASONING: Because within-firm normalization removes static value and profitability tilts, the resulting spread should carry small HML/CMA/RMW loadings and thus retain FF5 alpha while sorting on genuinely firm-specific news.
